title: Slimline Performance Snapshot: Model vs Route Heatmap & Token Funnels
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a compact, scannable performance snapshot card for the Redwood Console that surfaces per-model and per-route latency, throughput, token metrics and cost signals. The card should be usable in route and model lists, in a light-weight dashboard, and in an inspector rail. Focus on density, readability at small sizes, and progressive disclosure to more detailed charts.
acceptance_criteria: Card fits a 320x160 tile and an expanded 720x360 inspector canvas without layout breakage
Heatmap lane shows per-model percentile latency bands (P50/P95/P99) for the selected time window
Throughput sparkline shows request/s with an optional histogram overlay for burst events
Token funnel visualization displays input_tokens -> generated_tokens -> cached_tokens and computes cost-per-response
Chart styles match Console color tokens and remain colorblind-safe (passes WCAG contrast when a11y mode enabled)
Prototype links to an interactive drilldown: clicking a lane reveals micro-traces and the last failing request payload
Design handoff includes component specs, responsive rules, and Figma tokens for color/spacing
design_notes: Primary surface: slim tile used in route list. Secondary surface: inspector modal with more rows and mini-traces.
Use compact sparkline + tiny numeric for P50/P95 with micro-chevron to expand into waterfall or micro-trace view.
Heatmap encoding: vertical lanes per model variant or route; color intensity maps to median latency; outline shows P95 band.
Token funnel uses stacked bars with absolute token counts and a small cost badge deriving USD/token estimate from Optimize profiles.
Prefer stroke-based sparklines to preserve legibility at 1x pixel grids; reserve filled areas for larger canvases.
Progressive disclosure: show summary metrics first (latency/throughput/cost), then on hover reveal distribution and examples.
Accessibility: provide text alternatives and keyboard navigation for the drilldown; high-contrast toggle to swap palette.
Performance constraints: avoid expensive canvas redraws for lists — prefer SVG with throttled updates for live tiles.
Mobile behavior: collapse heatmap into stacked summary rows and surface expand control to view full lanes.
Edge case: when cache hits dominate, surface a prominent 'cache rate' metric and recommended action (increase TTL, warm prefixes).
review_feedback: PM (Ava Singh): prefer single-row P95 highlight color to match alerting thresholds; add clear CTA to create a rollout policy from card.
Engineering (Noah Patel): request that density options map cleanly to telemetry payload sizes; provide a fallback static image for very high-card counts.
SRE (Dana Ruiz): add an optional small error-rate spark next to throughput to quickly see reliability tradeoffs.
Design Review (internal): tighten the spacing between micro-sparklines to avoid optical crowding; increase token-label legibility at 10px font.
Accessibility Review (Ally Team): confirm keyboard focus traps inside inspector and that color palette passes 3:1 for non-critical elements and 4.5:1 for important metrics.
